_comment: Cross-language parity fixtures. Every entry is run through BOTH engines by parity/compare.py and the canonical digests (ENGINE_SPEC 9) are compared field by field. The set is chosen for COVERAGE, not realism: every aircraft, both aisle counts, one and two doors, all three door-assignment policies, open seating with each of its four seat-choice policies, the load-factor extremes, and the degenerate bag mixes -- because a draw-order bug usually shows up in exactly one of those corners. Fixture configs must use plain JSON-round-trippable values: the config_hash is a hash of the canonically re-serialised object, so an exponent or a 17-digit float would not survive the trip into JavaScript.

fixtures.name: a320neo_random_2door
fixtures._why: The house default and the calibration scenario: easyJet 186-seat single-class, both doors, random boarding.

fixtures.name: a320neo_wilma_1door
fixtures._why: Outside-in through a single door. Exercises the depth ordering and the zero-interference path.

fixtures.name: schultz_reference
fixtures._why: walkSpeedSd = 0 reduces the model exactly to Schultz's deterministic 0.8 m/s configuration, so this fixture is the apples-to-apples comparison against his published figures. Also the best structural regression canary in the set: it has no speed noise to hide a change behind.

fixtures.name: e175_starved_bins
fixtures._why: One bag slot per row-side against a regional bag mix: the gate-check and outward-bin-search paths, which nothing else in the set drives hard.

fixtures.name: b737_max8_lcc_two_door
fixtures._why: 197 seats, front and rear airstairs, deleted seats at rows 1/27/28 and a skipped row 13. The irregular-geometry fixture.

fixtures.name: a220_asymmetric_pyramid
fixtures._why: 2-3 asymmetric cabin: the port side can never produce a 9-movement shuffle, so this fixture pins the movement-count table on both sides at once.

fixtures.name: b777_twin_aisle_split_by_aisle
fixtures._why: Twin aisle, two doors, split_by_aisle. The only fixture where two lanes run in parallel with different door feeds.

fixtures.name: b777_steffen_single_door
fixtures._why: Steffen on a four-block twin-aisle cabin: 8 x maxDepth waves rather than the narrowbody's 4. Forces the generalised block indexing.

fixtures.name: b787_9_one_door_monuments
fixtures._why: Boards 2L only, with business forward of the door and economy aft, so the same lane carries traffic in both directions past three real galley monuments.

fixtures.name: open_seating_avoid_neighbours
fixtures._why: Seat choice made at the door line against the live seated set, plus the incremental nearest-neighbour distance cache.

fixtures.name: open_seating_window_first_two_door
fixtures._why: Open seating with more than one door, which falls back to round-robin door assignment because nobody has a seat to split on.

fixtures.name: empty_cabin
fixtures._why: loadFactor 0. Zero passengers must produce a well-formed zero-length result rather than a divide-by-zero.

fixtures.name: full_cabin_two_bags_everyone
fixtures._why: 100% load, everyone carrying two pieces, no zero-bag passengers. Saturates the bins and maximises the number of Weibull draws per passenger.

fixtures.name: no_bags_no_frictions
fixtures._why: The degenerate end: nobody has luggage, nobody is in a party, everybody complies. Isolates the aisle exclusion model from every service-time draw.

fixtures.name: single_passenger
fixtures._why: One passenger on a 354-seat aircraft: no queue, no blocker lookups, every counter at its floor.
